description: Imagine the aroma of freshly baked Focaccia Genovese filling your kitchen, its golden crust glistening with olive oil and fragrant rosemary. This classic Ligurian flatbread is wonderfully soft and chewy, with a delightful salty crunch from the coarse salt. Perfect as an appetizer, a side to any meal, or simply enjoyed on its own.

ingredients.notes: plus more for greasing and drizzling

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the warm water, yeast, and sugar. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active. This is crucial for a light and airy focaccia.

instructions.title: Mix the Dough
instructions.text: Add the flour and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Stir with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. Incorporate 2 tablespoons of olive oil into the dough. It will be sticky.

instructions.title: First Rise
instructions.text: Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp cloth and let the dough rise in a warm place for 1 to 1.5 hours, or until it has doubled in size. This slow rise develops flavor.

instructions.title: Prepare for Baking
instructions.text: Generously grease a 9x13 inch baking pan with 2 tablespoons of olive oil. Gently transfer the risen dough to the pan, being careful not to deflate it too much. Use your fingertips to gently stretch the dough to fill the pan.

instructions.title: Second Rise and Dimpling
instructions.text: Cover the pan and let the dough rise again for 30 minutes. After this, gently press your olive oil-dampened fingertips all over the dough to create the characteristic dimples. Drizzle generously with the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil, sprinkle with chopped rosemary and coarse sea salt.

instructions.title: Bake the Focaccia
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 220C (425F). Bake the focaccia for 20-30 minutes, or until it is golden brown and cooked through. The internal temperature should be around 90C (195F).

instructions.title: Cool and Serve
instructions.text: Once baked, remove the focaccia from the oven and carefully transfer it to a wire rack to cool slightly. Drizzle with a little extra virgin olive oil before slicing and serving warm. Buon appetito!

tips: Use good quality extra virgin olive oil for the best flavor, especially for the final drizzle. It makes a significant difference.
Do not over-knead the dough; focaccia benefits from a relatively wet and sticky dough for its characteristic texture. Gentle handling is key.
For extra crispiness, try baking on a preheated pizza stone or baking steel. Serve warm, perhaps with a side of good balsamic vinegar for dipping.
